top_stories.title: No more late salaries? UAE sees 151% jump in payroll processing as private-sector firms rush to meet new deadline - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **UAE** authorities have implemented a new wage payment rule requiring private sector employers to pay salaries on the first day of each month. This change, outlined in Ministerial Resolution No. 340 of 2026, has led to a significant increase in payroll processing activity across the private sector.  The **UAE Central Bank** and **Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE)** jointly oversee the Wage Protection System (WPS), designed to ensure timely wage payments and strengthen compliance monitoring. The new rule has impacted small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) requiring them to adapt their cash flow planning and payroll schedules.  The implementation is part of broader UAE efforts to strengthen labour market governance, safeguard employee rights, and standardize wage payment practices across the private sector.

top_stories.title: Indian national Gurpinder Singh arrested for attempting to steal $495,000 in gold bars from elderly Florida woman - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: A 20-year-old Indian national, **Gurpinder Singh**, was arrested in Florida after attempting to collect nearly $495,000 worth of gold from an elderly Gainesville woman. The scam began when the woman received a fraudulent email claiming her credit card had been compromised and instructed her to convert her money into gold.  **Singh** traveled from California to Florida to assist with the scheme, ultimately being arrested at a Chevron petrol station after attempting to collect the gold.

top_stories.title: 'Panic, uncertainty': Indian techie recalls moment when friends asked him to leave his own wedding and fly to US - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump**'s announcement of a $100,000 fee for H-1B visa petitions created uncertainty and panic among foreign-born workers in the US.  The fee was initially unclear who would pay it, leading to fears that all non-US citizens with H-1B visas would be subject to the charge. **Trump** administration later clarified that companies hiring after the announcement date would bear the cost. The situation has left many foreign-born workers feeling uncertain about their status in the US and prompting them to consider returning to their home countries.

top_stories.title: Indian man killed in Sharjah after alleged TikTok dispute turns into fatal attack | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Sharjah Police** confirmed the death of **Ismail Ponnan Ibrahim Kutty**, a 40-year-old Indian expatriate, following an alleged altercation linked to a TikTok dispute. The incident occurred near a park in Al Nahda on May 31st and involved multiple suspects who allegedly attacked **Kutty** after a disagreement during a livestream.  Police have arrested several individuals but haven't released further details about the case or those detained. Investigations are ongoing.

top_stories.title: Former US ambassador calls Indians corrupt, says America typically does not have fraud - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Carla Sands**, former US ambassador to Denmark, made controversial remarks on a podcast hosted by **Steve Bannon**, claiming that Americans are superior due to their adherence to the Ten Commandments and lack of fraud.  **Daniel Di Martino**, an immigration policy expert, condemned Sands' statement, arguing that Indian immigrants succeed through hard work and legal means, not fraud. He refuted Sands' claims about Indian fraud and emphasized that fraud does not benefit anyone in the long run.

top_stories.title: Ahmed Al-Ahmed: Bondi attack hero Ahmed al-Ahmed charged with assaulting father: Report - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ahmed al-Ahmed**, a man who was widely praised for disarming an attacker during last year's Bondi Beach shooting, has been charged with assault in Sydney. **Police** received a report of an alleged assault at a home in Bankstown on March 9, 2026, and subsequently charged a 44-year-old man with common assault and stalking. The man is scheduled to appear before Bankstown Local Court on June 29. He has denied the allegations.

top_stories.title: 'Cocaine-fuelled' Brit jailed for life over murder of Saudi student Mohammed Algasim in Cambridge | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Chas Corrigan**, a 22-year-old UK man, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 22 years and six months for the murder of **Mohammed Algasim**, a Saudi Arabian student.  Corrigan admitted consuming alcohol and cocaine before the attack, which occurred outside Cambridge railway station in August 2025. The court heard that CCTV footage captured Corrigan approaching the group before stabbing Algasim in the neck. Algasim's father and sister gave emotional statements during the sentencing hearing. **Peter Corrigan**, Corrigan's father, was sentenced to two years for assisting an offender. Cambridgeshire Police Chief Inspector Dale Mepstead stated that the sentence reflected the seriousness of Corrigan's actions.

top_stories.title: Former NSA-turned-Trump critic, John Bolton to plead guilty over retaining classified documents: Report - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **John Bolton**, former **US President Donald Trump's** national security adviser, is expected to plead guilty to mishandling classified documents. He plans to pay a fine exceeding $2 million and will receive a sentence ranging from zero to 60 months in prison. The plea agreement comes after the FBI discovered diary-style entries containing highly classified information from Bolton's time as national security adviser.  The case was reopened during the Biden administration following suspected Iranian hackers breaching his email account.

top_stories.title: Assam Cabinet expansion: Several new faces, no room for high-profile Congress defectors | India News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Sarma**'s cabinet has expanded to 17 ministers, with 12 of them from his first term.  The new additions include **Biswajit Daimary**, the Speaker of the previous assembly and a Bodo leader; **Nilima Devi**, president of the Assam Pradesh BJP Mahila Morcha; and **Ashwini Roy Sarkar** and **Sushanta Borgohain**. Notably, no high-profile Congress leaders who joined the BJP before the election have been included. The expansion leaves room for two more ministers in future.
